messages:
Noah: quick note from today's smoke tests: requests that carry both a project cookie (cookie: project=proj-11) and an org API key in Authorization are sometimes being routed to the org pool. This causes per-project quota and latency dashboards to be inconsistent.
Jin: can you paste the minimal repro and where the cookie is injected (edge vs proxy)?
Noah: repro: client sets cookie `project=proj-11` and also includes `Authorization: ApiKey org:org-2:abcd`. In our test proxy the cookie is applied by our edge CDN after header normalization, so header-parsing happens before cookie parsing. Runtime picks header-parsed org as principal.
Priya: telemetry saw a similar anomaly during last week's load test. Project-level SLOs showed low token counts while org-level usage spiked. We need a deterministic precedence rule.
Noah: my proposal: introduce a canonical "scope priority" config: cookie_project_hint > explicit_project_key > service_account_with_acting_claim > org_key. Also log `auth.candidate_list` and `auth.final_scope` as tags on traces.
Jin: implementation concerns: (1) changing precedence can change cache hit ratios. We should bake scope into cache keys: e.g. `auth:v4|scope:{type}:{id}`. (2) cookies are weaker auth; we should only honor cookie_project_hint if request also proves possession via project key OR request comes from trusted proxy.
Noah: agree on cookie safety. We'll only treat cookie hint as priority when `X-Trusted-Proxy: true` exists or when paired with an ephemeral project token. Otherwise cookie is low-priority.
Priya: for observability: add a single Prometheus counter `redwood_auth_resolution_total{outcome="project|org|sa|hinted"}` and a tag `auth.candidate_chain` for traces. Create a dashboard that shows per-project billing delta during canary.
Maya: from product: we must avoid blindsiding customers. If we flip precedence defaults, project owners might see sudden usage increases. Recommendation: gate change behind an org-admin toggle in the console and run a 7-day slow rollout with billing-delta monitoring. Also surface a short banner when the org toggles it.
Jin: ok feature flag `auth.scope_priority_v2` default=false. Add a runtime canary rollout tool that compares current and proposed attribution for sampled requests (store diff counts).
Noah: tests: unit for precedence logic, integration that replays recorded requests with edge ordering permutations, and a billing-diff job in staging that runs nightly.
Priya: I'll wire alerts: if sampled billing-delta > 4% for any project during canary, we rollback. Also add an alert for if `auth.candidate_chain` contains more than 1 candidate in >5% of requests (signal ambiguous auth patterns).
AlertBot: canary-deploy initiated by @priya  id=cny-2026-03-21-77 target=4% traffic in us-east1. Logs will go to #build-failures.
Noah: created ticket infra/auth-scope-priority-2026 and opened runtime PR with flag + cache namespace changes. Will follow up with console PR for admin toggle and banner.
Maya: I'll draft banner + short FAQ for support. Copy suggestion: "Attribution update: we're improving how requests with multiple auth signals are assigned to projects or orgs. You may see temporary changes to project usage while this rolls out. Learn more."
Jin: also add a staging-only compatibility flag that preserves old ordering for regression tests.
Noah: great. Updating ticket with action items and ETA: canary today, monitor 24h, then expand to 25% if stable.
